session.title: Foundry Product Strategy Review
session.description: Judge whether the app ends with the right recommendation and whether every UI surface represents that outcome accurately.

transcript.content: Our product vision is an AWS-native advisory app that can simulate, review, and improve coding-agent deployments. We need one default recommendation the app can defend, and we want the review to show whether the UI itself is telling the truth.

The recommendation is now complete. For this product, the right default is **Codex on Bedrock** inside the managed AWS control plane, with `Claude Code` kept as a deferred alternative rather than the primary recommendation.

I published the final brief, the architecture, and the technical blueprint so the UI can be reviewed as a finished session instead of an in-progress draft.

workspace.recommendation: Standardize this app on Codex on Bedrock as the default recommendation path. It fits the AWS-native control plane, keeps model access, auditing, and deployment review inside the same governed environment, and leaves Claude Code as a non-default comparison or exception lane rather than the lead answer.
workspace.blueprint_markdown:
## Technical Blueprint

### Product Outcome
The app runs as an enterprise review workbench that can inspect a deployment, score the resulting recommendation, and surface the open items a reviewer should act on.

### Default Recommendation Path
- Default coding harness: Codex
- Model and governance path: Amazon Bedrock
- Runtime posture: managed AWS execution with policy, logging, and report capture inside the same control plane
- Exception posture: Claude Code may be evaluated as a deferred alternative, but not as the default answer for this product

### Review Workflow
1. Capture the product vision and target deployment context.
2. Simulate the session and persist the visible workspace state.
3. Judge the outcome against the product vision and UI accuracy rubric.
4. Publish the recommendation, architecture, blueprint, open items, and feature suggestions.

### UI Accuracy Rules
- The Brief must show the real recommendation and confidence.
- The Questions panel must reflect only active blockers.
- The Blueprint tab must clearly distinguish published artifacts from synthesized drafts.
- The Architecture board must expose the control path, execution boundary, and reporting surfaces.

### Rollout
1. Add deterministic review scenarios and a golden-path seeded session.
2. Add LLM-as-judge reports driven by product vision and UI outcomes.
3. Add live deployment review and persisted session playback in the normal app UI.

facts: The product is AWS-native and already uses Bedrock-aligned deployment primitives.

decisions: Recommend Codex on Bedrock as the default product strategy for this app.

workspace.blueprint_markdown:
## Technical Blueprint

### Target State
A governed multi-harness platform with two execution lanes: a shared standard lane for most engineers and a regulated lane for in-region repositories that require stricter approval and audit ownership.

### Control Model
- Shared discovery, policy, and model-routing standards.
- Separate approval workflow and audit ownership for the regulated lane.
- Common observability with region-specific telemetry storage.

### Rollout
1. Pilot the standard lane for non-regulated teams.
2. Stand up the regulated lane with isolated execution and approvals.
3. Expand the operating model under shared governance.
facts: Twenty percent of repositories are regulated and must stay in-region.
A shared standard lane is still required for the broader engineering population.
Regulated teams need separate approvals and audit ownership.
decisions: Use a governed multi-harness operating model instead of forcing one standard tool on all populations.
Separate the regulated execution lane with its own approval and audit path while preserving shared platform governance.
risks: If shared policy definitions and regulated-lane controls drift apart, the platform will become operationally expensive and inconsistent.
The regulated lane may experience slower onboarding unless approval workflows are automated early.
implementation_plan: Pilot the standard lane with non-regulated teams in the next 30 days.
Stand up the regulated lane with isolated execution, approvals, and telemetry within 90 days.
Unify policy, quota, and observability reporting across both lanes within 180 days.

recommendation.summary: Adopt a governed multi-harness platform with one shared standard lane and one separately governed regulated lane.
recommendation.why_this: It preserves broad developer access while containing regulated workloads inside the correct execution, approval, and audit boundaries.
recommendation.why_not: A single standard lane would violate the control boundary, while fully separate platforms would duplicate governance and fragment the developer experience.
recommendation.confidence_reason: The primary execution, identity, and residency decisions are now resolved.
change_triggers: A new class of workloads requires a third isolated lane.
Shared model routing is no longer allowed for the regulated population.

readout.architecture_snapshot: Shared surfaces and governance feed two execution lanes with common model-routing standards.

output_pack.executive_summary: The enterprise should adopt a governed multi-harness platform that keeps the standard lane broadly accessible while isolating regulated repositories inside a separately approved in-region execution path.
output_pack.recommendation_memo: This model balances developer scale with the control boundary. It avoids forcing one compromised standard across incompatible populations.
output_pack.architecture_narrative: Users enter through shared surfaces and governance. Requests for standard workloads flow through the shared lane, while regulated workloads are routed into a separately approved in-region path with independent audit ownership.
key_decisions: Use a governed multi-harness operating model.

Keep shared observability, quota, and policy standards.

Separate approval ownership only where the control boundary requires it.
